questions.q: What is a reconciliation rule set?
options: The named group of matching (and optional tolerance) rules attached to a bank account
A type of BAI2 transaction code
questions.explain: A reconciliation rule set is the top-level object attached to a bank account, grouping the matching rules (and optional tolerance rules) it uses.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the components a matching rule specifies?
options: Matching criteria such as amount and date
questions.explain: A matching rule specifies transaction source, match type, group-by attributes, and matching criteria — not a branch's physical address.

questions.q: A single lump-sum bank deposit that needs to match against several individual Receivables receipts is an example of which match type?
questions.explain: One to Many matches a single statement line against a group of several system transactions, exactly this lump-deposit scenario.

questions.q: A tolerance rule associated with a matching rule can only apply when the matching rule's match type is which of these?
questions.explain: Tolerance is only applied when the matching rule is a One to One match type; other match types don't support an associated tolerance.

questions.q: Why might two different bank accounts use two different reconciliation rule sets?
options: Rule sets are randomly assigned by Oracle at setup time
Because different account types, like payroll versus general AP, may need to match transactions differently
Because only one rule set can ever exist per company
Because reconciliation rule sets expire after 90 days
questions.explain: Different account types reasonably need different matching behavior, so different accounts can be assigned different rule sets.
